# DnsPro v1.0.0

The first stable release of **DnsPro**, a C++23 library for parsing,
building, and resolving DNS messages against an in-memory authoritative
zone.

## Highlights

- **RFC 1035 wire-format packet structs** — `Header`, `Name`, `Question`,
  `ResourceRecord`, and `Message`, under `DnsPro::Packet`, giving parsed
  DNS messages a typed, structured representation rather than raw bytes.
- **`Parser`: bytes → `Message`** — offset-driven, single-pass parsing,
  with DNS name-compression pointer support (RFC 1035 §4.1.4) including
  rejection of forward/self-pointers and pointer loops
  (`Status::COMPRESSION_FORWARD_POINTER`, `Status::COMPRESSION_LOOP`).
- **`Builder`: `Message` → bytes** — always writes full, uncompressed
  names. This is a deliberate simplification, not a correctness gap:
  round-trip correctness only requires that a rebuilt packet re-parse to
  an equivalent `Message`, not that it match another encoder's
  compression choices byte-for-byte.
- **`ZoneStore`** — an in-memory, case-insensitive (RFC 4343) authoritative
  record store, indexed `name → type → records` so lookups don't
  degrade as the zone grows.
- **`Resolver`** — ties `Parser` + `ZoneStore` + `Builder` into a single
  `resolve()` call: raw query bytes in, raw response bytes out, with
  correct NOERROR/NXDOMAIN/NODATA handling.

## Performance

- Nested `name → type → records` indexing in `ZoneStore` keeps
  `lookup()` and `removeRecord()` cost independent of zone size —
  measured flat at ~144 ns/op whether the zone holds 100 or 10,000
  names.
- `Message` move-construct/move-assign cost ~5–10 ns regardless of how
  many questions or answer records the message holds, since `Vector`'s
  move steals the underlying buffer pointer rather than copying
  elements.
- Compression-pointer following in `Parser::parseName()` adds real,
  bounded overhead over an uncompressed name — the one place
  decompression cost shows up directly in the numbers below.

## Benchmarks

Solo-timed at 10K / 100K / 1M iterations — no reference implementation
exists to compare against (there's no standard-library or widely-used
DNS parser/zone-store to pair each benchmark with). Full results:
`benchmarks/results/v1.0.0.md`.

| Operation | DnsPro (1M) |
|---|---|
| `Parser::parse()` — query, single question | 62.97 ns/op |
| `Parser::parse()` — response, 4 answer records | 296.11 ns/op |
| `Builder::build()` — query, single question | 122.20 ns/op |
| `Builder::build()` — response, 4 answer records | 399.52 ns/op |
| `ZoneStore::lookup()` — existing name+type | 137.71 ns/op |
| `ZoneStore::lookup()` — missing name | 61.89 ns/op |
| `Resolver::resolve()` — answer found | 448.81 ns/op |
| `Resolver::resolve()` — NXDOMAIN | 360.46 ns/op |
| `Message` move-construct | 5.99 ns/op |
| Name parse — uncompressed | 63.46 ns/op |
| Name parse — via compression pointer | 96.05 ns/op |

The full `Resolver::resolve()` pipeline (360–449 ns/op) is the most
expensive path, unsurprising since it chains parse, zone lookup, and
build together — each stage individually stays under 400 ns/op.
`ZoneStore` lookups stay essentially flat at ~144 ns/op from 100 names
up to 10,000, confirming O(1) hash-based lookup rather than
degradation with zone size. The clearest trade-off is name
compression: resolving a name through a compression pointer costs
~51% more than an uncompressed name (96.05 ns vs. 63.46 ns/op) — the
added cost of following the pointer hop.

## Testing

The project includes a comprehensive test suite — both the custom
framework and GoogleTest, covering the same categories — spanning:

- Unit tests
- Integration tests
- Lifecycle tests
- Regression tests
- Concurrency tests

`ZoneStore` currently has no internal locking, so its Concurrency test
deliberately exercises the real unsynchronized write race rather than
asserting correctness — see the Concurrency test suite for details.

## Code Coverage

The current test suite achieves:

- **89.2% line coverage** (265 / 297 lines)
- **86.2% function coverage** (25 / 29 functions)

Coverage figures exclude test infrastructure and third-party
dependencies (GoogleTest/GoogleMock, vendored submodules), focusing on
the DnsPro library implementation.

## Continuous Integration

Automated builds and tests are configured for:

- GCC — Debug
- GCC — Release
- Clang — Debug
- Clang — Release
- MSVC — Debug
- MSVC — Release
- AppleClang — Debug
- AppleClang — Release

## Release

This release establishes DnsPro's complete core API surface: typed
wire-format structs, bidirectional parse/build with compression-pointer
support, an authoritative in-memory zone store, and a resolver tying
them together into a single raw-bytes-in, raw-bytes-out call. It does
not include a transport/network layer, and `ZoneStore` is not yet safe
for concurrent writes without external synchronization — both are
known, documented gaps rather than oversights.

## Installation

**From source:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/privateMwb/DnsResolver.git
cd DnsResolver
cmake -B build \
  -DBUILD_TESTS=OFF \
  -DBUILD_BENCHMARKS=OFF \
  -DBUILD_REGRESSION=OFF \
  -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF
cmake --install build
```

Then, in your own `CMakeLists.txt`:

```cmake
find_package(<CMAKE_PACKAGE_NAME> CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(your_target PRIVATE <CMAKE_PACKAGE_NAME>::<CMAKE_PACKAGE_NAME>)
```
